newsitem.title: USA: U.S. judge denies Gambia millionaire immunity.
newsitem.headline: U.S. judge denies Gambia millionaire immunity.

text.p: A U.S. federal magistrate has ruled that a West African millionaire who pleaded guilty to a charge of bribing a U.S. customs officer may not claim diplomatic immunity.

In a ruling handed down late on Thursday, Magistrate Ted Bandstra found that Foutanga Dit Babani Sissoko, a citizen of Mali and Gambia, "is not immune from prosecution as a result of his designation as a Special Advisor on a Special Mission for the Gambia."

"Unfortunately, and for reasons never fully explained, the Gambia never properly notified the United States Department of State of Sissoko's designation as a diplomatic officer or member of its diplomatic mission in the United States," he wrote.
Sissoko, who faces a sentence of 45 days imprisonment and four months of home confinement, has 10 days to appeal the latest ruling in his case.
He pleaded guilty in January to paying a $30,000 bribe to a U.S. customs agent in a bid to ship two military helicopters to Gambia.

Gambia had petitioned the Miami U.S. District Court to overturn his conviction on the grounds that he was serving as a special envoy for that country and had diplomatic immunity from criminal prosecution.
A host of African nations condemned the case against Sissoko, who heads a company called Negoce International and is known for his largesse in West Africa and Miami.

Following his conviction, he gave $60,000 Mercedes cars to each of his three lawyers, tens of thousands of dollars to a Miami high school marching band and a gold watch and $10,000 cash to a masseuse who went to his condominium but was not allowed to touch him because of his religious beliefs, according to press reports.
